links.outcome: Hallucination reduction and F1 when grounding LLM answers in UMLS knowledge graph versus other LLM methods
links.effect: Hallucinations drastically reduced; F1 of 91.1% (MedQA) and 86.0% (custom dataset) with domain-fine-tuned models; KG-validated data with fine-tuned models performed best among LLM methods.
links.quote: Evaluating on MedQA and Custom biomedical dataset for various tasks, our method drastically reduced hallucinations and achieved F1 rates of 91.1% (MedQA) and 86.0% (our dataset) with domain-fine-tuned models like Llama-3.1-8B-UltraMedical.

unlisted_practices: Three-phase query-checking module (syntactic, semantic schema compatibility, logical relationship integrity) for LLM-generated Cypher queries against a knowledge graph
Prompt engineering and algorithmic optimization to bring open-source models close to closed-source accuracy

screen.reason: The study tests an architecture/safeguard practice (combining LLMs with structured knowledge graph retrieval grounding and a multi-phase query verification module to prevent hallucinations) on medical question-answering benchmarks (MedQA and a custom biomedical dataset).

primary.practice: knowledge graph grounding with query refinement checking
